content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Guides gumroad

Gumroad, Stripe, and PayPal are popular choices for creators, offering a range of services, including payment processing, order management, and delivery. However, these platforms come with limitations and restrictions. Gumroad, for example, charges a 3.5% + $0.30 per sale fee, while Stripe operates in only 46 countries, leaving creators in restricted countries with limited options. PayPal, on the other hand, can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, posing a significant risk to creators who rely on timely income.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, each option handles the situation differently. Gumroad has a list of supported countries, and creators in unsupported countries are forced to use alternative payment methods or workarounds. Stripe operates in a limited number of countries, leaving creators in restricted countries without access to its services. PayPal, while available in many countries, has strict policies and can suspend accounts at any time, leaving creators without a payment solution.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

In terms of payment speed, fees, and real costs, each option has its pros and cons. Gumroad's fees are transparent, but the payment processing speed can be slow. Stripe's payment processing speed is fast, but its fees can be high, especially for creators who process small transactions. PayPal's fees are complex and can vary depending on the transaction type and country. When considering these factors, it's essential to look beyond the initial fees and understand the real costs of each option.
A sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround, but a permanent solution for creators who want to maintain control over their digital sales.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When it comes to ownership, automation, and delivery, each option has its strengths and weaknesses. Gumroad allows creators to maintain ownership of their products, but the automation features are limited. Stripe offers robust automation features, but creators must integrate these features themselves. PayPal's automation features are limited, and creators often have to rely on third-party integrations. A sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, allows creators to maintain full ownership and control over their products, automation, and delivery.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

Platform restrictions are not a customer service problem — they are an infrastructure problem. You cannot solve an infrastructure problem by calling support or finding the right contact at Stripe or PayPal. You solve it by building on infrastructure that was not designed around those restrictions in the first place. NOWPayments operates on blockchain rails — it has no correspondent banking relationships, no AML corridors to approve, and no geographic risk model that flags your country. It verifies transactions on-chain and fires a webhook. Your Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script receives the webhook and processes the order. The entire sequence is independent of any conventional financial institution.

Your Deployment Checklist

Stop using a friend's account in another country — this violates platform terms and puts both accounts at risk. Create a NOWPayments merchant account under your own email — no KYC required, takes under 15 minutes. Configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron as your primary coin and Bitcoin as your secondary. Deploy your backend — Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App — and confirm the endpoint URL is accessible. Set the endpoint URL as the webhook URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings with the secret key configured in both places. Build or deploy your storefront on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. Run a mainnet test transaction — send a small amount of real USDT to your configured address, confirm the webhook fires, the order logs, and the delivery email arrives. Promote your store only after the complete test passes.
